original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: First compare the alphabet, role count and length with the fully replayed #1974 census and #2027 mixed-root tariff. Identify a changed premise and a legal native implementation; then price one smallest completed instance before searching larger words.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.
Repeating the two-register GL3 census or a covered three-register length without changing a hypothesis; a formal group-algebra word without native conversion is a partial result.

actual_scope: Existence of a complete no-edge binary rank-one idempotent pool of pattern dimension 5 whose joint image has dimension 7 and is irreducible.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for a larger or nonabelian register alphabet. This package stays in the abelian F2 rank-one idempotent model and answers open question 1 of #7139: whether a complete no-edge pool of pattern dimension 5 still has total joint image at most 6, and whether its irreducible image can exceed 5. No new alphabet, word, or kappa is claimed. The same card was already moved to scalar pattern-pool questions by #5921, #6838, #6921, #6962, and #7094.
bottleneck_link: Side result. The scalar pool does not by itself price a word, so the original native acceptance gate remains unmet. A later word argument can no longer assume that every pattern-dimension-5 no-edge pool has total image at most 6 or irreducible image at most 5. The selected frontier is unchanged.
stop_rule: Stop once the seven-projector pool is identified at every width at least 7 and its action is proved irreducible, with the parity column recorded as the reducible comparison of total image 6. Do not start an upper-bound proof or a coordinate classification.
evidence: PROOF.md shows that the seven explicit projectors are the complete pool of a unit-free pattern space of dimension 5, that the joint image has dimension 7, and that the action is irreducible. verify.py repeats the pattern arithmetic, the width scans, the 127-vector closure, and the deleted-link and parity controls.

open_questions.question: Does every complete no-edge pool of pattern dimension 5 have total joint image at most 7?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The seven-projector witness shows that 6 is too small, while the zero-edge quotient bound is still 31. A matching upper bound would make 7 sharp.
open_questions.first_step: Show that a unit-free one-dimensional extension of a dimension-6 no-edge pattern space adds at most one image dimension.
open_questions.blocked_by: The extension estimate is not proved in this package. A width-bounded search would not be a proof.

open_questions.question: Is every irreducible complete no-edge pool of pattern dimension 5 and joint-image dimension 7 a coordinate permutation of the seven projectors exhibited here?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The existence proof does not say whether another linking geometry reaches the same dimension.
open_questions.first_step: Match the two normal-form blocks and the linking vector to the coordinates used here.
open_questions.blocked_by: Section 7 of the proof uses one linking vector and does not classify other links.
